title: Only some courts were collected again after January 2019
evidence: Recorded decisions run at about 10 lakh a month through 2018, fall to about 1 lakh a month by April 2019, and a trickle continues to September 2020. Follow-up therefore differs by court.
treatment: Every case is treated as open on 31 Dec 2018 unless decided by then, so no court gains from later collection. See docs/methods.md.

title: Early years are under-covered
evidence: Rows per filing year rise 3.2x from 4.28M (2010) to 13.72M (2018). Litigation did not triple, so this reflects the spread of digital records.
treatment: Flow rates use 2016-2018 only. Survival results are also reported by filing year because older cohorts look slower.

title: Disposals of pre-2010 cases are absent
evidence: The data holds only cases filed from 2010, so disposals of older cases are never counted, which understates disposals in every state.
treatment: Clearance rates and years-to-clear are stated as lower bounds and used for comparison between places, not as forecasts.

title: Five NJDG states and UTs have no separate DDL rows
evidence: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Andaman and Nicobar have no DDL rows. Puducherry and Lakshadweep appear only as districts under Tamil Nadu and Kerala, so their state rows cannot be compared.
treatment: Listed in the Coverage sheet. Excluded from state rankings where they have no DDL flows.

title: NJDG '>5 years' column is mislabelled
evidence: In Lok Sabha Q.3371 Annexure II, West Bengal shows more cases over 10 years (8,05,149) than over 5 years (7,19,828), so the column cannot be cumulative.
treatment: Stored as 5-10 years. A unit test checks the assumption and the printed totals.

title: DDL district crosswalk is incomplete
evidence: 96 of 630 DDL districts have no Census 2011 link and one (Delhi South East) is linked to the wrong district.
treatment: Hand-built crosswalk of 96 rows with a link type for each, plus one correction. Districts carved after 2011 count towards their 2011 parent so per-lakh rates stay honest.

title: Four 'districts' are statewide tribunals
evidence: Maharashtra's family courts, school tribunals, industrial and labour courts and cooperative appellate court appear as district codes.
treatment: They stay in state totals and are left out of district per-lakh figures.

title: Metadata does not match the files
evidence: female_petitioner is in the files but not the data dictionary. Gender columns use two formats ('0 male' and bare 0). The judge key is named ddl_filing_judge_id rather than the documented ddl_judge_filing_id.
treatment: Loader parses both gender formats, and docs/data_dictionary.md records the real schema.

title: Public files contain a linkable case number
evidence: cino (the eCourts case number) is present in the public case files, although the DDL page says identifiers need a separate request.
treatment: Dropped at load and never stored in Parquet, so no output can link back to a named case.

title: Act key counts look rounded
evidence: act_key lists 'The Indian Penal Code' at exactly 20,900,000, a rounded value from a float column.
treatment: Volumes are recounted from the case rows, and the key's counts are not used.

title: Some acts look like dropdown defaults
evidence: Acts such as 'Absorbed Areas (Laws) Act' and 'Acquired Territories (Merger) Act' carry tens of thousands of cases each and about 4 lakh together. Their names sit near the top of an alphabetical list and district courts rarely apply them.
treatment: Grouped as 'Implausible act' in Q3 rather than treated as real law. The cause is inferred, not proven.

title: A loose matching rule misfiled 1.8M cases
evidence: An early act-name pattern ('nact$') also matched every squeezed name ending in '-ion act', which sent Land Acquisition, Dowry Prohibition and similar acts to the NI Act.
treatment: Caught by a unit test before any result was used. Fixed, with regression tests for each affected act.

title: Project plan citations did not match their source
evidence: The plan cites the eCourts India blog for a 1-2% of GDP cost and 30-40 lakh Section 138 cases. The blog says 0.5-1.5% and 54 lakh+ (a full-text index count), and never mentions 30-40 lakh.
treatment: The brief uses the blog's actual range and tests Section 138 against the Supreme Court's 35.16 lakh figure (31 Dec 2019) as well as the blog's count.

title: Gender is predicted from names
evidence: DDL infers gender with a neural network on names and reports 97% accuracy on samples. The label is male or female only and many names are unclassifiable.
treatment: Share of women is computed on classified names only and the unclassified share is always shown. It should not be read as a count of individuals.

title: Some districts appear to have incomplete closure records
evidence: In a small group of districts, led by Bihar, almost no case closes within two years, even bail matters, which normally close within days. That points to unrecorded closures rather than slow courts.
treatment: Flagged with a bail-based check. Flagged districts are left off rankings and shaded as no data on the map, and each affected state's median is also reported without them.

title: Act records are thin for early years
evidence: Act links cover about half of cases filed 2010-2012 but 94-97% from 2015. Overall 14.8M cases (18%) have no act record. The act table also has about 9M rows for 2019-2020 cases with no matching case file.
treatment: Shown as 'No act record' in Q3 and never redistributed. Section 138 is tested both by act and by case-type label.

title: Women's shares count cases rather than people
evidence: The same advocate appears on many cases, and the name is often unclassifiable: only 13% of defendants' advocates and 46% of petitioners' advocates have a usable label.
treatment: Reported as a share of classified cases, with the unclassified share shown beside it.

title: A join shortcut lost about 4M act links
evidence: To speed up the join, an early version narrowed the acts table by the last four digits of the case ID, assuming they were the filing year. They differ from it in 8.5% of cases. A left join keeps its row count, so the row-count check passed.
treatment: Caught when reviewing link rates by year, before any result was used. Joins now use the full ID, and integrity tests check the match rate, not just the row count.

title: Verdict labels are too uneven to compare states
evidence: Only about 30% of criminal closures record a conviction or acquittal, and the share runs from under 10% in some states to over 60% in others. A state conviction rate built on this would mostly measure labelling.
treatment: Verdicts are reported by case type only and are never ranked by state.

title: Judge postings may be split by court number
evidence: A posting is one judge in one court position, so moving between court numbers in the same complex counts as a new posting. That can shorten the measured time in a post, and states may record it differently.
treatment: Reported as time in a post rather than time in a court. It is used for scale and not ranked in any finding.

title: The licence in the download differs from the licence on DDL's website
evidence: The license.txt inside the data archive is the Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0, while DDL's data page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and asks commercial users to request a separate licence.
treatment: This project follows the stricter terms on DDL's page: attribution, non-commercial, share-alike. The archive's text is kept in docs/ddl_license_in_archive.txt. Ask DDL before any commercial use.
